summaries.n-gta6-launch-coins: Coins named for Grand Theft Auto VI. Twenty-three coins are measured, each with GTA in its name or description: WASTED ("the iconic GTA death screen"), GTA6CAT, GTA Dollars, Ah shit, here we go again. ("The most iconic GTA meme of all time, with GTA 6 coming out"), gtacoin (LaunchLab; "the one coin for all of gta"), Macca The Gator ("GTA 6 Mascot"), State of Leonida ("The home state of GTA VI"), Peekhole ("a parody of OnlyFans inside GTA 6"), GTA memes, Jason Duval (named for a GTA VI protagonist; it says holders earn $TTWO stock, which is not verified here), Bawsaq (GTA's fictional stock exchange, "from the world of GTA 6"), Rocco, EEAGLE and Mission Passed (from 2026-11-06), and, from 2026-11-16, GRAND THEFT CRYPTO ("The first GTA server with real cryptocurrency"; its account describes a GTA-style role-play server, not verified here), Doug The Frog ("the frog... from Macca the Gator..., the cartoon inside GTA 6") and Cyber Dacity Coin ("GTA-inspired chaos to neon Miami"), and, from 2026-11-17, three coins named for BAWSAQ, the games' fictional stock exchange: Vice City Index ("BAWSAQ is the GTA VI stock index on Solana") on Pump.fun and a Meteora DBC copy of the same name, and Vice City Bawsaq; Leonida Games ("Built for the players waiting on Leonida"); Grand Theft Anthropic (symbol GTA, a pun that posts call GTA-inspired); and Here We Go Again (symbol GTAVI). All but gtacoin (LaunchLab) and the Meteora DBC Vice City Index are on Pump.fun. Dates from Codex: the GTA6CAT and GTA memes pools opened in late August 2026, Macca The Gator, Jason Duval, Peekhole, EEAGLE and WASTED in October, and the other sixteen between 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-17, all ahead of the release. Coins named only for the in-game Dacity Coin brand are a separate narrative, paused on 2026-11-16. None of the coins is shown to be connected to Rockstar Games or Take-Two. Measured: twenty-three coins across all their pools.
summaries.n-nvidia-ceo-scandal: Coins named for the Nvidia CEO story. The New York Times posted on X on 2026-11-08 that Nvidia opened an investigation into its CEO Jensen Huang after he acknowledged to the board a relationship with a business executive whom U.S. intelligence determined to be a Chinese spy. On 2026-11-11 The Wall Street Journal posted that Nvidia's board was preparing to oust him. On 2026-11-12 at 13:57 UTC Yahoo Finance posted that Huang had resigned as CEO and that CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO; a Reuters post of 2026-11-13 calls him the former Nvidia CEO and says the Justice Department has not concluded whether the businesswoman, Alice Huang, was a spy. On 2026-11-14 Polymarket posted that a petition to reinstate Huang had passed 100,000 signatures.
